name: 0.20mm Support Easy @Solder
notes: Easy-release variant of 0.20mm Standard @Solder. EXACTLY ONE VALUE DIFFERS: support_top_z_distance 0.4 instead of 0.2, which is two 0.2 mm layers of air under the part instead of one. Everything else is the proven geometry from the holder.3mf prints - tree(auto) organic, support_interface_top_layers 0, support_interface_bottom_layers 2, support_base_pattern_spacing 2.5, support_object_xy_distance 0.35, support_line_width 0.38, support_on_build_plate_only 1, support_critical_regions_only 1. READ THIS BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING ELSE: an earlier attempt at snap-off supports cut interface layers to 0, widened the gaps, thinned the support lines AND switched to tree_slim all at once, and the towers collapsed in the first few layers. This preset moves one variable from the proven set so a failure names its own cause. The trade is the underside finish. Two layers of air means the first bridged layer over a support has further to span, so it sags more and the scar is rougher even though the support lifts off with less force. If the underside matters more than the removal effort, use 0.20mm Standard @Solder. UNTESTED - no print has run on this preset. The gap is layer-aligned deliberately: 0.3 would be one and a half layers and Klipper prints the nearest layer boundary, so the real gap becomes whichever side it rounds to.
